title: Octopus facts: three hearts, blue blood and thinking arms
description:
An octopus has three hearts, copper-based blood and about 500 million neurons, most of them in its arms. A quick look at why people say an octopus thinks with its arms.
#shorts #octopus #nature #animalfacts

scenes.narration: An octopus has three hearts. And that's not even the weirdest part.
scenes.imagePrompt: underwater shot of an octopus spreading its arms over a coral reef, light rays from above, deep midnight blue palette with cyan highlights, cinematic lighting, shallow depth of field, no text

scenes.narration: Two hearts pump blood through the gills. The third, the main one, sends it around the whole body.
scenes.imagePrompt: close-up of an octopus mantle and tentacles in dark water, bioluminescent glow, deep midnight blue palette with cyan highlights, cinematic lighting, shallow depth of field, no text

scenes.narration: And its blood is blue. Oxygen isn't carried by iron, like ours. It's carried by a copper protein called hemocyanin.
scenes.imagePrompt: a single glowing blue drop falling into dark water, macro, deep midnight blue palette with cyan highlights, cinematic lighting, shallow depth of field, no text

scenes.narration: When an octopus swims, its main heart stops. That might be why it crawls along the bottom more often than it swims.
scenes.imagePrompt: octopus crawling across a sandy sea floor, soft caustic light patterns, deep midnight blue palette with cyan highlights, cinematic lighting, shallow depth of field, no text

scenes.narration: But the most amazing part is the nervous system. An octopus has about five hundred million neurons. That's one of the most complex nervous systems among invertebrates.
scenes.imagePrompt: glowing neural network shaped like octopus arms, dark background, deep midnight blue palette with cyan highlights, cinematic lighting, shallow depth of field, no text

scenes.narration: And about two thirds of them aren't in the head. They're right in the arms.
scenes.imagePrompt: octopus arms with faint glowing nerve lines inside them, deep blue water, deep midnight blue palette with cyan highlights, cinematic lighting, shallow depth of field, no text

scenes.narration: Each arm largely feels and grabs things on its own, and even tastes them with its suckers. In a way, an octopus thinks with its arms.
scenes.imagePrompt: macro of octopus suckers gripping a seashell, crisp detail, deep midnight blue palette with cyan highlights, cinematic lighting, shallow depth of field, no text

scenes.narration: Which animal do you think is the weirdest? Tell me in the comments.
